robot: aerial manipulator: a fully actuated hexarotor (six tilted rotors) carrying a 4-joint arm with a two-finger gripper (AM-Bench on Isaac Lab)

frame.suite: the task's world frame: z up, the ground is the plane z = 0, positions relative to the environment's origin
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: at the airframe's centre (measured at the start of each call), +X the airframe's heading, +Y to its left, +Z straight up (level: the heading only, the airframe's tilt is ignored); it moves with the airframe

arm.note: the end effector of the whole robot: AM-Bench's whole-body controller places the airframe and the arm's 4 joints so that the tool frame reaches the pose (you command where the end effector should be; the airframe follows); gripper -1 = closed .. +1 = open in AM-Bench's own scale

ee.point: the tool frame tcp (the end-effector link ee_link)
ee.mode_text: a pose target for AM-Bench's whole-body controller (floating-base IK, rotor thrust PID, arm joint drives) every 120 Hz control step; rows are interpolated at a moderate speed and the robot follows with some lag

notes: The robot flies: there is no separate base command, the airframe moves wherever the end-effector target needs it (base_odometry in each result is the airframe's world position and heading). At the start the airframe hovers level facing +X with the arm at its zero joints and the gripper closed. Move in small steps and watch the cameras: the airframe, not only the arm, approaches nearby surfaces. The state's gripper value is the command in force; gripper_opening_m is the measured finger opening (0.002 m = closed on nothing). The episode ends by itself at the first control step where the task is done, or at the task's episode length of simulated time (spec_file max_control_steps at 120 Hz).
